title: Worker liveness as one explicit state machine, its timings from one table
description: Worker liveness ties an advisory lock, a nodes row and job leases together through eight timing constants; keepRow mixes registration, relock and lost-lock handling, DOMAINS 25 is about 4,000 words, and every recent change here risked stopping every transcode. After JS-066's fault injection exists, rewrite keepRow as states (locked, relocking, row gone) with each timing derived from the lease in one table, and cut DOMAINS 25 to that table. Keep the measured 4 s takeover.
acceptanceCriteria: Worker liveness (keepRow and what Present does around it, internal/transcode/liveness.go) is one state machine: its states are named in code (at least locked, relocking and row gone; registration, the lock held and the row not yet inserted, is a named state or a named transition), every transition is named with its event, and the next state for a state and an event is decided in one place that the unit tier can ask with no Postgres.

The transitions are today's and no others: locked to relocking when the lock's connection ends; relocking to locked only once the lock is held again and the row is found there; locked or relocking to row gone when a look finds the row gone; locked to row gone when a look finds the worker's own lock missing from pg_locks while its connection stands; row gone to a new registration only after no job of the old session runs (waited for at most today's 10 s) and a new lock is held; any state to stopped on shutdown.

What each state allows is today's: only a locked worker claims jobs, forgets other workers and refreshes seen_at; a relocking worker's jobs go on with the same ffmpeg processes while it only reads its own row and retries the lock; entering row gone stops every transcode ffmpeg of the worker at once and those jobs end cancelled (interrupted), never failed; the row is inserted once per lock and never put back while relocking.

A look or a registration that Postgres does not answer within its bound is no event in any state: nothing is stopped, nobody is forgotten, and it is tried again at the next look; a worker still registers over a database that takes 300 ms a round trip.

A look runs every look period and also at once, not at the next tick, on each of: the lock's connection ending, a forgot hint for this worker, and the moment a node first seen lockless has been so for the confirmation gap.

A locked worker forgets another only when all three of today's conditions hold (the node's lock gone in two of its looks at least the confirmation gap apart, its own lock held in the same snapshot, its own lock not ended within the hold), for one dead worker and for several at once; a relocking worker and a replica forget nobody and delete no row.

A worker holds at most one liveness connection and runs at most one relock loop at any time, however often its lock connection is ended; after Present returns from any state, mid-relock included, its row is deleted and it holds no liveness lock or connection.

One table in code names every worker-liveness timing, each written as an expression of the default lease and not as a duration of its own; at the 10 s lease each has exactly today's value, no longer and no shorter: lease 10 s, heartbeat and seen_at refresh 3 s, worker counted if seen within 10 s, grace (also the longest a refusal waits on a lockless worker) 1 s, lease left to a forgotten worker's jobs 0.5 s, confirmation gap 0.5 s, bound of a look, row check or refresh 0.5 s, look period 0.25 s, relock retry 50 ms, hold after the worker's own lock ended 10 s.

No duration that decides when a worker looks, retries, gives up a wait, is forgotten or stops counting is written outside that table: none in liveness.go, not the wait in Unavailable or workerAlive in jobs.go, not the 3 s that cmd/jellyscale/main.go passes to Present.

The table is the cluster's, not a worker's: a worker run with another Lease (the tests use 3 s, 20 s, 30 s and 1 min) changes only its jobs' lease, as today, and its liveness timings, Reap's and a replica's stay those of the table at the default lease.

DOMAINS 25 holds the same table as the code, row for row with the same name, the same derivation from the lease and the same value at 10 s, and the states with their transitions; a check fails when a row, derivation or value is changed in the code or in DOMAINS.md alone.

DOMAINS 25 is shorter than today's 811 words, and DOMAINS.md still states every guarantee invariant 25 states today: every job has a kill path and no ffmpeg outlives its lease; losing the lock is not losing the lease; the three conditions for forgetting; a replica forgets nobody; a worker without its row claims, renews and stores nothing; one row per lock; no replacement starts while the old ffmpeg runs, with its stated bound on a slow database; a worker killed during an outage is forgotten up to the hold later; a job ended because Postgres was away is cancelled, never failed; a worker that only lost its lock lets a subtitle extraction finish.

Every existing liveness test (internal/transcode: liveness_test.go, failover_integration_test.go, outage_integration_test.go, idle_replica_outage_integration_test.go, segment_wait_outage_integration_test.go, TestAKilledWorkersJobIsClaimedBeforeItsLeaseRunsOut, TestAWorkerReapedByItsOwnLookIsCounted) and every JS-066 test (faultplan_test.go, faults_integration_test.go, faults_docs_test.go, stop_scope_integration_test.go, claim_race_integration_test.go, stopped_past_stall_integration_test.go) passes with the test process, its worker processes and their ffmpeg held to two CPUs, and the unit tier passes.
None of those tests is deleted, skipped or loosened: each keeps every assertion and every bound it has today, and changes at most the name of a constant or function the rewrite renamed.

Takeover is no slower, shown by mechanism and never by a measured duration: with a second worker free, a SIGKILLed worker's job is claimed by the other before the dead worker's own lease runs out (at leases of 10 s and 30 s), Reap leaves a forgotten worker's running jobs at most the table's 0.5 s of lease, and the time from the kill to the claim is logged, not asserted.

Refusal is no slower: with the last worker killed, a replica's Unavailable waits on the lockless worker no longer than the table's 1 s grace before it answers that no transcode worker is running, deletes no row, and answers without that wait when no counted worker is lockless.

Liveness costs Postgres no more than today: one liveness connection per worker; a locked worker's look is at most two round trips that write nothing unless a node is forgotten, plus the seen_at refresh once per heartbeat; a relocking worker's look is one read of its own row.

The operator's log is today's: the messages liveness.go logs now for the lock's connection ending, a lock Postgres does not show (naming the transaction-mode pooler), being forgotten by another replica, and holding the lock again are logged at the same transitions, once per transition.
